body:
Tuta raised the minimum client version its API accepts. Anything reporting a
`cv` major below 357 now gets `474 InvalidSoftwareVersionError`. The vendored
SDK reports `348.260528.0`, so login fails for everyone on `main` — it dies in
the SDK's `fetch_server_model`, the first call that reaches the server, before
any credential goes out.

    [INFO tutabridge] TutaBridge starting...
    [INFO tutasdk] Initializing SDK...
    Password for you@tutanota.com:
    [INFO tutabridge_core::tuta] Authenticating with Tuta servers...
    Attempting to get base model version?  2
    Error: Login failed: ApiCall: ServerResponseError: Invalid Software Version

You don't need a real account to see it — the rejection lands before
credentials are checked, so a nonexistent address and a junk password get you
the same error.

Where the cutoff sits, bisected against `base/applicationtypesservice`
(unauthenticated, `v: 2`):

    348.260528.0   474
    355.260720.0   474
    356.260806.1   474
    357.260812.1   200
    359.260904.0   200

Refused through 356, accepted from 357 up. Sampled repeatedly over several
minutes — it's a hard cutoff, not flapping.

Only the client version is gated. The `v` model header isn't: `base` is still
2, and `sys/saltservice` with `v: 150` vs `v: 154` returns the same non-474
either way. So the client type models being stale (`sys` 150 vs 154,
`tutanota` 108 vs 114, `storage` 14 vs 15) isn't the problem here, and nothing
needs regenerating.

Fix is one line — `CLIENT_VERSION` is `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` and nothing
else reads the workspace version. Two PRs, in order:

1. tutanota (`tutabridge-integration`) — raise the workspace version
2. tutabridge — move the submodule pointer onto it

The second can't build until the first merges.

Worth noting this will come back. Tuta moves the floor every few months, and
no offline test can see it coming: the full suite passes at `348.260528.0`
while login is completely broken. A network smoke test asserting the current
`CLIENT_VERSION` still gets a non-474 from `base/applicationtypesservice`
would catch the next one before users do.
